news.story_lead: Climate-linked heat deaths rise 36% since Paris Agreement; India also affected: Lancet People in India were exposed to over 2,600 hrs per yr during which heat posed a moderate or higher risk of heat stress during moderate outdoor physical activity The health impacts and risks of climate change accelerated in the decade since the Paris Agreement entered into force (2016–2025) indicating climate action failed to keep pace, the 10th indicator report of the Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change has found. The report added that high heat remained a concern for India in the decade 2016-25, with the Lancet report stating people in the country were exposed to over 2,600 hours per year during which heat posed a moderate or higher risk of heat stress during moderate outdoor physical activity. This figure is over 200 hours higher than the annual average in the 1990s.
news.full_article_text: Climate-linked heat deaths rise 36% since Paris Agreement; India also affected: Lancet People in India were exposed to over 2,600 hrs per yr during which heat posed a moderate or higher risk of heat stress during moderate outdoor physical activity The health impacts and risks of climate change accelerated in the decade since the Paris Agreement entered into force (2016–2025) indicating climate action failed to keep pace, the 10th indicator report of the Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change has found. The report added that high heat remained a concern for India in the decade 2016-25, with the Lancet report stating people in the country were exposed to over 2,600 hours per year during which heat posed a moderate or higher risk of heat stress during moderate outdoor physical activity. This figure is over 200 hours higher than the annual average in the 1990s. “People in India also lost an estimated 64 hours of sleep annually, due to high night-time temperature between 2021 and 2025, approximately three hours more per year than 1986-2005,” it added. Released on Wednesday, the report said the annual average heat-related deaths worldwide has increased by nearly 36% in the decade since the Paris Agreement came into force, with human-caused climate change responsible for more than 70% of the record 710,000 heat-related deaths reported in 2023 alone. The report, led by University College London (UCL), and produced in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO), calls for climate change to be formally recognised as a global health emergency, with health placed at the centre of decisions on emissions reduction, adaptation and climate funding. Also Read: COP31 success is about delivery, support and scale, not new targets: Bhupender Yadav Heat deaths and extreme weather risks The Paris agreement, which came into force in 2016, asked countries to limit global warming well below 2°Celsius and preferably to 1.5° Celsius, compared to pre-industrial levels. However, the UN’s own assessment earlier this month, showed if current policies continue, global warming could reach 2.8°C within this century and increase thereafter. “Heat was linked to an average of 540,800 estimated deaths per year between 2016 and 2023, 68% of them (369,900) caused by climate change, up from 55% (219,100) per year in 2006–2015. In 2023 alone, the hottest year in that period, heat was linked to a record 710,000 estimated deaths, exceeding those from malaria or HIV, with 71.5% of them driven by climate change. Altogether, climate change is estimated to have caused almost 3 million heat deaths between 2016 and 2023,” stated the Lancet report. High heat levels have also led to extreme drought in parts of the world, affecting nearly 52% of the world’s land for at least a month in 2025 – the second-highest level on record, the Lancet said, adding a satellite-based analysis suggests since 2003, 80% of the world’s land has faced significant shifting patterns of increasing dry and wet groundwater storage conditions, with implications for food security and sanitation. Also Read: Unprecedented climate crisis hit on India: Study It said since 2016, the area affected by drought has grown more than 700% faster than it did in 2006–2015. “At the same time, very extreme rainfall is also becoming more common, reaching almost 17.2% of global land each year in 2016–2025, up from 14.8% the previous decade, and increasing the risk of floods, landslides and waterborne disease,” the report said, stating climate extremes add to the health risk. The report represents the work of 146 multidisciplinary researchers from more than 100 institutions across more than 30 countries. Published ahead of the 31st UN Conference of the Parties (COP31), tracks 54 indicators of the health impacts of climate change and the health effects of climate action, including four new indicators introduced this year covering the availability of water in land, healthcare sector greenhouse gas footprint assessments, climate-related health research funding, and legislative engagement with health and climate change. Also Read: Govt submits draft of its new climate plan Health at the centre of climate action “A decade after the Paris Agreement, our findings are unambiguous: the health harms of climate change are growing faster than the world’s response to them, and in many cases even accelerating,” says Professor Marina Romanello, Executive Director of the Lancet Countdown, based at University College London. The report states that despite gains in the health care system, overall progress is falling short. “Cleaner energy, more resilient health systems, along with more health-protecting legislation and growing scientific evidence have brought real health benefits to local communities since the 2016 Paris Agreement, but these gains are still too slow, too insufficient, and too inconsistent to offset the growing risks, states the study. The findings carry particular significance for India, where recurring heatwaves pose serious risks to outdoor workers, older people, children and those with existing health conditions, stated the study . Extreme heat can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially fatal heatstroke, while also aggravating cardiovascular and respiratory illnesses, states the report. The report’s authors warn that the health benefits of cleaner energy and better preparedness are being undermined by the continued expansion of fossil fuels and insufficient investment in adaptation. “The rate of increase in many climate-related health threats is accelerating, while heat deaths linked to climate change have reached a record-high, and the economic toll is battering vulnerable sectors and communities the hardest,” said Marina Romanello, executive director of the Lancet Countdown. Clean energy gains and calls for action On the flipside, the report said the transition to clean energy has helped prevent a significant number of deaths and represents a pathway countries need to take globally. Worldwide, clean energy investment reached a record US$2.1 trillion in 2025 – almost double what was invested in fossil fuels, it said. news.full_article_text: UAPA does not bar bail for all foreigners; illegal entry is key, rules SC The court said the statutory bar applies only when a foreigner has entered India unauthorisedly or illegally The Supreme Court on Tuesday ruled that the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) does not impose a blanket prohibition on granting bail to foreign nationals accused under the anti-terror law, clarifying that the statutory bar applies only when a foreigner has entered India unauthorisedly or illegally, and not merely because their subsequent stay in the country becomes unlawful. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi held that the prosecution must prima facie establish that an accused is not an Indian citizen and that their initial entry into India was unauthorised or illegal to trigger the stringent restriction under Section 43D(7) of the UAPA. A foreign national who entered India legally on a valid visa cannot be brought within the provision merely because the visa subsequently expires or the person’s stay becomes illegal, held the court. The ruling came as the court dismissed an appeal by the Union government challenging a Madras high court order that restored bail to Mohamed Rifas, a Sri Lankan national accused in a case being investigated by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) over an alleged conspiracy to disturb communal harmony, wage an armed struggle against the government and to liberate their associates lodged in prisons. “The appellant has failed to place any material on record to prima facie establish the entry as unauthorized or illegal,” said the bench, noting that the allegations in a separate FIR against Rifas indicated that he had entered India on a valid visa and that his stay became illegal only after the visa expired. The court underscored that Section 43D(7) imposes a high threshold for bail where its conditions are met, given considerations of national security, public interest and India’s sovereignty. The provision allows bail in such cases only in “very exceptional circumstances”, with reasons recorded in writing. “The legislative intent warranting such high threshold is primarily backed by considerations of national security, larger public interest and sovereignty of India,” said the bench, adding that the burden of establishing very exceptional circumstances would lie on the accused. Section 43D of the UAPA imposes stringent restrictions on bail in terror-related offences, including a bar on anticipatory bail and a requirement that courts deny bail in certain cases if the accusations are prima facie true; Section 43D(7) sets an additional, higher threshold for foreign nationals who entered India illegally or without authorisation, permitting bail only in very exceptional circumstances and for reasons recorded in writing. The case arose from an FIR registered in Tamil Nadu in April 2018, accusing Rifas and others of conspiring to incite communal discord and engaging in activities punishable under the UAPA and other laws. He was granted default bail in July 2018 after the investigating agency failed to file a chargesheet within the prescribed statutory period. The NIA subsequently took over the investigation and filed a chargesheet in January 2021. A separate FIR was registered in November 2019 alleging that Rifas was a Sri Lankan national who had overstayed his visa and fraudulently obtained Indian identity documents, including a voter ID card and Aadhaar. In April 2022, the Union government sought cancellation of his bail, arguing that he had concealed his foreign nationality when seeking release and that Section 43D(7) barred bail to foreign nationals accused under the UAPA. The special court cancelled his bail in July 2022, but the Madras high court reversed that decision in December 2023. The Supreme Court rejected the Centre’s contention that the alleged suppression of nationality justified cancellation of bail. It emphasised that Rifas had been granted statutory default bail under Section 167(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, a right that also applies to UAPA cases through Section 43D(2) of the Act. The bench held that the overriding effect and restrictions of Section 43D(7) do not override the provision governing default bail. Consequently, even if the foreign-national restriction were otherwise attracted, it would not displace the statutory entitlement to default bail. The court also found that the Centre had failed to establish a compelling basis for cancelling the bail after the chargesheet was filed. While the chargesheet was submitted in January 2021, the application seeking cancellation was moved only in April 2022, and the government had not satisfactorily explained the delay. The bench reiterated that cancellation of bail is distinct from setting aside an order granting bail. While bail may be cancelled for post-release misconduct or supervening circumstances, a superior court can also interfere with an original bail order if it is legally unsustainable, perverse or based on irrelevant considerations. Such powers, however, must be exercised with caution because personal liberty carries substantial constitutional value. news.headline: Chief Justice Surya Kant Issues New Roster Widening Case Allocation Across Supreme Court Benches
news.story_lead: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has notified a new subject-wise roster for the Supreme Court, expanding the diversity of case categories assigned across individual judicial benches. Effective October 26, the updated allocation reshuffles the previous July 13 roster to distribute commercial, civil, environmental, regulatory, and constitutional matters across a broader set of judges.
news.full_article_text:
### Judicial Roster Reshuffle
Under the directions of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, the Supreme Court has issued a revised roster governing the distribution of fresh cases among its benches. The new allocation system, which came into force on October 26, modifies the previous subject roster introduced on July 13. The revision broadens the mix of litigation assigned to individual judges—encompassing commercial disputes, direct taxation, competition law, insolvency, environmental laws, family disputes, and land acquisition—while maintaining overlapping subject domains across multiple benches.

### Detailed Changes in Bench Allocations
- **Justice MM Sundresh:** Expanded to include company law, competition law, direct taxation, educational institutions, environmental law, insolvency and bankruptcy (IBC), land acquisition, and land laws, alongside existing allocations in civil/criminal law, election disputes, labour, and service matters.
- **Justice Vikram Nath:** Roster now includes arbitration, aviation, banking, company law, compensation, competition law, and consumer disputes, complementing his existing civil, criminal, environmental, and service law matters.
- **Justice Dipankar Datta:** Assigned family law, habeas corpus, preventive detention, land acquisition, land laws, lotteries, betting, and gambling, alongside general civil, criminal, commercial, and taxation matters.
- **Justice PS Narasimha:** Allocation expanded to cover matters regarding bar councils, bar associations, advocates, family law, housing and municipal issues, and judiciary-related cases, in addition to arbitration, company law, taxation, and intellectual property disputes.
- **Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra:** Assigned company law, competition law, consumer disputes, direct taxation, environmental law, insolvency, mining, and land-related matters, alongside criminal and service litigation.
- **Justice Aravind Kumar:** Roster covers arbitration, banking, competition, consumer disputes, direct taxation, education, environmental law, insolvency, mining, religious endowments, and service matters.
- **Justice Sandeep Mehta:** Included in the roster for fresh cases, receiving civil law, consumer disputes, criminal law, capital punishment cases, labour law, motor vehicle disputes, rent control, service law, and transfer petitions.

### Expansion of Habeas Corpus Benches and Dedicated Bench Allocation
- **Habeas Corpus & Preventive Detention:** The number of benches assigned to hear habeas corpus and preventive detention matters has doubled from four to eight. Added to the existing benches (headed by CJI, Justice Vikram Nath, Justice BV Nagarathna, and Justice MM Sundresh) are benches headed by Justices Dipankar Datta, Aravind Kumar, Prashant Kumar Mishra, and KV Viswanathan.
- **Three-Judge Matters:** Benches headed by the CJI, Justice Vikram Nath, and Justice BV Nagarathna will primarily handle three-judge bench matters on non-miscellaneous days (Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday).
- **Targeted Backlog Management:** Dedicated benches have been assigned long-pending regular-hearing cases to avoid competition with fresh filings:
  - *Oldest Service Matters:* Bench led by Justice Dipankar Datta (on non-miscellaneous days).
  - *Oldest Civil Matters:* Benches led by Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and SVN Bhatti.
  - *Oldest Criminal Cases:* Benches led by Justices Manoj Misra and Ujjal Bhuyan.

### न्यायिक रोस्टर में फेरबदल
प्रधान न्यायाधीश सूर्यकांत के आदेशानुसार, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने अपनी पीठों के बीच नए मामलों के वितरण को नियंत्रित करने वाले विषय-वार रोस्टर में संशोधन किया है। 26 अक्टूबर से लागू यह नई आवंटन व्यवस्था 13 जुलाई के पिछले रोस्टर को संशोधित करती है। इस बदलाव के तहत वाणिज्यिक विवाद, प्रत्यक्ष कर, प्रतिस्पर्धा कानून, दिवालियापन (IBC), पर्यावरण कानून और भूमि अधिग्रहण जैसे विषयों को विभिन्न पीठों के बीच अधिक व्यापक रूप से वितरित किया गया है।

### प्रमुख न्यायाधीशों के आवंटन में बदलाव
- **जस्टिस एमएम सुंदरेश:** कंपनी कानून, प्रतिस्पर्धा कानून, प्रत्यक्ष कर, शैक्षणिक संस्थान, पर्यावरण कानून, दिवालियापन (IBC), और भूमि अधिग्रहण जैसे विषय नए शामिल किए गए।
- **जस्टिस विक्रम नाथ:** मध्यस्थता (Arbitration), उड्डयन, बैंकिंग, कंपनी कानून, मुआवजा, प्रतिस्पर्धा कानून और उपभोक्ता विवाद शामिल किए गए।

news.headline: India’s Record Banking Cash Surplus Shrinks as RBI Intervenes to Curb Rupee Speculation
news.story_lead: India’s banking system cash surplus, which had previously expanded to record levels, has begun to recede as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) takes action to restrain speculative bets against the Indian Rupee. The central bank's interventions have absorbed excess cash from the banking system while aiming to stabilize the domestic currency.
news.full_article_text:
### RBI Liquidity Operations and Foreign Exchange Intervention

India’s commercial banking sector has witnessed a contraction in its record surplus cash reserves following market steps taken by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The central bank moved to curtail speculative trading activity and derivative positioning directed against the Indian Rupee, leading to a drawdown of liquidity in the money market.

### Impact on Money Market Conditions

To counter exchange rate volatility and deter market participants from taking aggressive short positions on the Rupee, the RBI executed liquidity-absorbing operations. These interventions effectively drained excess funds from the banking channel, bringing down the historic liquidity surplus held by domestic banks while promoting balance in interbank cash conditions.

news.headline: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Concludes in New Delhi with Joint Declaration Targeting Terrorism and Calling for UNSC Reform
news.story_lead: The two-day 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum concluded in New Delhi with the adoption of a joint declaration advocating for United Nations Security Council (UNSC) reform, zero tolerance for terrorism, and enhanced representation of the Global South. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla presided over the meeting and formally transferred the forum's chairship to China for the 2027 summit cycle.
news.full_article_text:
### Event Overview and Parliamentary Governance
The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum convened in New Delhi on October 26 and 27, bringing together presiding officers and parliamentary representatives from BRICS member states and partner countries. Discussions centered around strengthening legislative institutions, integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into governance, and advancing sustainable development. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla stressed that enduring solutions to global challenges must stem from peace, collaboration, and respect for national sovereignty, rather than conflict and competition. He further emphasized that modern parliaments need to evolve beyond simple law-making into transparent, citizen-focused bodies leveraging AI and digital tools for advanced research and public engagement.

### UNSC Reforms and Global South Advocacy
The forum culminated in a comprehensive joint declaration reaffirming adherence to the United Nations Charter. Member nations advocated for structural reforms across the UN framework, specifically emphasizing the UN Security Council to enhance its equity, democratic representation, and operational efficiency. The declaration underlined the necessity of utilizing international legislative platforms, including the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), to elevate the voices and priorities of the Global South on international policy matters.

### Counter-Terrorism Framework and Regional Peace
Addressing global security concerns, the declaration forcefully condemned the terror attack in Pahalgam on April 22, 2025, which claimed 26 civilian lives. The joint statement urged strict compliance with a zero-tolerance policy regarding terrorism, calling for an elimination of double standards in counter-terrorism efforts. It mandated concerted global action against cross-border movement of terrorists, terror financing, and designated safe havens. Additionally, the forum expressed concern over rising tensions in West Asia and the Middle East, urging restraint and reiterating firm support for a two-state solution to resolve the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

### Technology, Sovereignty, and Climate Commitments
In the technology domain, the joint declaration proposed creating a dedicated Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) repository for BRICS members. It emphasized safeguarding national data privacy, personal information security, and technological resilience to protect digital sovereignty. Regarding environmental action, member countries recommitted to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development while maintaining the core principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) in climate mitigation and adaptation strategies. Finally, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla officially transferred the chairship of the forum to China ahead of the 2027 summit.

hindi_translation.story_lead: नई दिल्ली में आयोजित दो दिवसीय 12वां ब्रिक्स संसदीय मंच एक संयुक्त घोषणापत्र को अपनाने के साथ समाप्त हुआ। इसमें संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद (UNSC) में सुधार, आतंकवाद के खिलाफ जीरो टॉलरेंस और ग्लोबल साउथ के प्रतिनिधित्व को बढ़ाने की मांग की गई। लोकसभा अध्यक्ष ओम बिरला ने सम्मेलन की अध्यक्षता की और 2027 के शिखर सम्मेलन चक्र के लिए मंच की अध्यक्षता चीन को सौंपी।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### आयोजन का अवलोकन एवं संसदीय शासन
26 और 27 अक्टूबर को नई दिल्ली में आयोजित 12वें ब्रिक्स संसदीय मंच में ब्रिक्स सदस्य देशों और भागीदार राष्ट्रों के पीठासीन अधिकारियों तथा संसदीय प्रतिनिधियों ने भाग लिया। इस मंच का मुख्य ध्यान संसदीय संस्थाओं को सशक्त बनाने, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (AI) और डिजिटल प्रौद्योगिकियों के उपयोग तथा सतत विकास पर केंद्रित रहा। लोकसभा अध्यक्ष ओम बिरला ने अपने संबोधन में कहा कि वैश्विक चुनौतियों का स्थायी समाधान युद्ध के बजाय संवाद, संघर्ष के स्थान पर शांति और प्रतिस्पर्धा की जगह सहयोग से ही संभव है। उन्होंने इस बात पर बल दिया कि आधुनिक संसद को कानून बनाने से आगे बढ़कर एआई और डिजिटल उपकरणों के माध्यम से अनुसंधान एवं सार्वजनिक भागीदारी को बढ़ावा देने वाली पारदर्शी तथा नागरिक-केंद्रित संस्था बनना चाहिए।

### यूएनएससी सुधार और ग्लोबल साउथ का समर्थन
मंच का समापन संयुक्त राष्ट्र चार्टर के सिद्धांतों की पुनः पुष्टि करने वाले एक संयुक्त घोषणापत्र के साथ हुआ। सदस्य देशों ने संयुक्त राष्ट्र प्रणाली, विशेष रूप से सुरक्षा परिषद (UNSC) में व्यापक सुधारों का आह्वान किया ताकि इसे अधिक न्यायसंगत, लोकतांत्रिक, प्रतिनिधि और प्रभावी बनाया जा सके। घोषणापत्र में वैश्विक नीति-निर्माण में ग्लोबल साउथ की आवाज को बुलंद करने के लिए अंतर-संसदीय संघ (IPU) जैसे अंतरराष्ट्रीय मंचों के उपयोग पर जोर दिया गया।

### आतंकवाद विरोधी ढांचा और क्षेत्रीय शांति
सुरक्षा चिंताओं पर बात करते हुए, घोषणापत्र में 22 अप्रैल 2025 को पहलगाम में हुए आतंकवादी हमले की कड़े शब्दों में निंदा की गई, जिसमें 26 नागरिकों की जान गई थी। संयुक्त बयान में आतंकवाद के खिलाफ 'जीरो टॉलरेंस' नीति अपनाने और दोहरे मापदंडों को समाप्त करने की अपील की गई। इसने सीमा पार आतंकवाद, टेरर फंडिंग और सुरक्षित ठिकानों के खिलाफ निर्णायक कार्रवाई की मांग की। इसके अलावा, ब्रिक्स देशों ने पश्चिम एशिया में बढ़ते तनाव पर चिंता व्यक्त की और इजरायल-फिलिस्तीन संघर्ष के शांतिपूर्ण समाधान के लिए दो-राष्ट्र सिद्धांत के प्रति अपनी प्रतिबद्धता दोहराई।

### प्रौद्योगिकी, संप्रभुता और जलवायु प्रतिबद्धताएं
प्रौद्योगिकी के क्षेत्र में, संयुक्त घोषणापत्र में ब्रिक्स देशों के लिए एक समर्पित 'डिजिटल पब्लिक इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर' (DPI) रिपोजिटरी बनाने का प्रस्ताव रखा गया। इसमें डेटा गोपनीयता, व्यक्तिगत जानकारी की सुरक्षा और डिजिटल संप्रभुता की रक्षा पर जोर दिया गया। पर्यावरण के मोर्चे पर, सदस्य देशों ने 2030 सतत विकास एजेंडे को लागू करने और जलवायु परिवर्तन से निपटने में 'समान लेकिन विभेदित उत्तरदायित्व' (CBDR) के सिद्धांत का पालन करने की प्रतिबद्धता जताई। अंत में, ओम बिरला ने 2027 के शिखर सम्मेलन के लिए मंच की अध्यक्षता चीन को सौंप दी।

news.story_lead: SC castigates Centre over medicine overpricing, asks 'can you justify this loot' New Delhi, Flagging the "massive difference" between the MRP of medicines and the price to retailers, the Supreme Court on Tuesday slammed the Centre asking if it can provide "any justification for this loot" and also if manufacturers be allowed to "run amok". A bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta observed that the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority seems to be a "totally defunct" body and asked the government why the entire system was working to help pharmaceutical manufacturers. The top court reserved its verdict on two petitions which raised drug-related issues, including that of ensuring strict price control over medicines.
news.full_article_text: SC castigates Centre over medicine overpricing, asks 'can you justify this loot' New Delhi, Flagging the "massive difference" between the MRP of medicines and the price to retailers, the Supreme Court on Tuesday slammed the Centre asking if it can provide "any justification for this loot" and also if manufacturers be allowed to "run amok". A bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta observed that the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority seems to be a "totally defunct" body and asked the government why the entire system was working to help pharmaceutical manufacturers. The top court reserved its verdict on two petitions which raised drug-related issues, including that of ensuring strict price control over medicines. Deep Dive After the Centre told the bench about the decision to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the maximum retail price , the bench asked why there can't be a uniform 16 per cent margin on all medicines. "The government policy is that entire ecosystem is not to be controlled," Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, told the bench. The bench observed that a medicine having ₹ 15 as price to retailer , carries an MRP of ₹ 250. "Can you show any justification for this loot," the bench asked, adding, "The government is allowing this to happen. It is under the government's own eyes that it is happening." When Bhati referred to the aspect of having control, the bench asked, "Should it be allowed to run amok?" The law officer told the bench that medicine prices in India were among the lowest in the world. While referring to the difference between the MRP and PTR, the bench said, "Why is the entire system working to help these people ." The top court referred to a recent case where a medical distributor's wife was admitted to a hospital for cancer treatment. It said the hospital charged ₹ 1.30 lakh for an injection which was available at a price of ₹ 11,000 to the distributor. "It seems that the public at large is living in some day dream that some day they will be benefitted by the NPPA," the bench observed. NPPA was constituted as an independent regulator for pricing of drugs and to ensure availability and accessibility of medicines at affordable prices. When Bhati referred to the issue of control, the bench observed, "It is not a question of control. There is 300 per cent, 400 per cent or more difference. Why this difference? Where does that difference go? What is the justification for this massive difference." The law officer referred to the Centre's affidavit which said the Indian drug market is fairly competitive, with a large number of pharmaceutical companies in every drug segment, resulting in one of the lowest prices in the world. When Bhati stressed on the need for a calibrated approach, the bench observed that patients don't have the bargaining powers and they have to shell out exorbitant price for medicines. "We wish every medicine is considered as generic medicine," the bench said. It also questioned the Centre why it took so long to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the MRP. "Only after we started putting questions, the government has woken up and now you are saying we have done this," the bench told the law officer. Bhati also referred to the aspect of growth of the pharmaceutical industry. "You are talking about commerce and economic policy. Don't weigh patients against commerce," the bench said. "When we talk of patients and their lives, can we look at it with a capitalist view?," it asked. While hearing the matter on October 12, the top court had said the Centre's response on capping the trade margin of anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the MRP was "hardly anything to be happy about" and questioned why the government cannot cap trade margins of other medicines. The Centre, which had earlier come under severe criticism from the top court for steep markup of cancer drugs by hospitals, said that the government has taken an important decision to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the MRP, which is expected to result in annual savings of approximately ₹ 2,500 crore to patients. The bench had said that the Centre's response was insufficient and flagged that a single saline drip was sold in market for ₹ 270 while its actual cost was ₹ 11. One of the petitions sought a direction to the authorities to make drug formulations more cost-effective by preventing alleged unethical overpricing of essential medicines by pharma companies and retailers. It also sought directions to ensure strict price control under the Drugs Order, 2013, to prevent violations of the price-fixing mechanism in the drug supply chain and disproportionate profit-making by retailers through unfair trade practices. The other plea has sought disciplinary action against medical practitioners for not prescribing generic medicines to patients. Cyclone Arnab's landfall process started along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday around 1:10am, bringing strong winds and heavy rainfall to several areas, the Indian Meteorological Department said. In its bulletin issued at 1.10am on October 28, the IMD said Arnab’ was moving westwards over the west central Bay of Bengal, close to the Andhra Pradesh coast and Yanam, at a speed of 10 kmph.
news.full_article_text: Cyclone Arnab starts landfall process along Andhra Pradesh coast, triggers heavy rain and strong winds Authorities remain on high alert as rescue and relief teams continue to take precautionary measures to minimise the impact of the severe cyclonic storm. Cyclone Arnab's landfall process started along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday around 1:10am, bringing strong winds and heavy rainfall to several areas, the Indian Meteorological Department said. In its bulletin issued at 1.10am on October 28, the IMD said Arnab’ was moving westwards over the west central Bay of Bengal, close to the Andhra Pradesh coast and Yanam, at a speed of 10 kmph. IMD estimated the storm’s intensity at 125-135 kmph, with gusts reaching 150 kmph. The storm is expected to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam , south of Yanam, between 2 am and 4 am. Winds are likely to gradually weaken after landfall. Track live updates on Cyclone Arnab Authorities remain on high alert as rescue and relief teams continue to monitor the situation and take precautionary measures to minimise the impact of the severe cyclonic storm. Andhra Pradesh and Odisha had stepped up preparations on Tuesday ahead of the expected landfall of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, with thousands of people moved to safety, nearly 4,000 cyclone shelters readied and at least 50 trains cancelled across the region. Air travel impacted Air travel was also affected, with at least 21 flights cancelled at Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam airports on Tuesday. The cancellations affected services to Chennai, Bengaluru, Visakhapatnam and Kadapa. An official said 15 flights scheduled to operate from Vijayawada airport on Wednesday had also been cancelled. Also read: Cyclone Arnab: Why Bay of Bengal storms tend to form after the monsoon Andhra Pradesh ensures preparedness The Andhra Pradesh government had arranged 2,131 cyclone shelters across 20 districts and placed 1,087 medical teams on standby in areas likely to be affected. Officials said 8,281 emergency beds and 1,274 ambulances had also been made available. Deep Dive Authorities had moved people out of vulnerable areas and shifted 1,351 pregnant women to hospitals. The government had stocked two months' worth of essential commodities at 14,686 ration shops, while cyclone alerts had been sent to the mobile phones of 2.70 crore people. Railways monitored 600 km of tracks, cancelled services The South Coast Railway had cancelled 24 trains scheduled for Wednesday, while the East Coast Railway had cancelled 22. The South Eastern Railway had also cancelled four trains, officials said. IMD director general Mrunjay Mohapatra had warned of potentially damaging winds along the coast. Odisha had moved over 30,000 people to cyclone shelters Odisha had intensified its preparations, with heavy rain already reported in parts of the state. Schools had been closed in 16 of its 30 districts, while more than 30,000 people had been moved to cyclone shelters against a target of 48,000, a revenue department official said. Entry to sea beaches had been prohibited. Special Relief Commissioner (SRC) Rajesh P Patil said 135 permanent cyclone shelters and around 1,600 temporary shelters had been prepared to accommodate people from vulnerable areas. Jharkhand had shut schools, issued yellow alert In neighbouring Jharkhand, the Ranchi district administration had ordered schools to remain closed on October 28 and 29 as authorities prepared for adverse weather. A yellow alert for heavy rain had been issued for Ranchi, Khunti, Simdega, Gumla, Lohardaga, Saraikela-Kharsawan, East Singhbhum and West Singhbhum for 24 hours from 8.30 am on October 28. The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum concluded in Delhi on Tuesday with the adoption of a joint declaration backing reform of the United Nations Security Council, calling for zero tolerance for terrorism and greater representation of the Global South in global decision-making. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also handed over the forum’s chairship to China for the next BRICS summit in 2027. “Permanent solutions to global challenges can only be forged through dialogue, not war; in peace, not conflict; and in collaboration, rather than competition,” Birla said in his address. He further called for a global framework based on respect for national sovereignty, peaceful resolution of disputes and equitable development opportunities. Also read: Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla urges Brics parliaments to turn dialogue into concrete outcomes The forum— held on October 26 and 27 under the theme “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development”— brought together presiding officers and parliamentary representatives from BRICS member countries and partner nations. It focused on strengthening parliamentary institutions, the use of artificial intelligence and digital technologies and sustainability. The forum was held during India’s 2026 BRICS chairship, which had the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”. The joint declaration reaffirmed the principles of the United Nations Charter and called for comprehensive UN reform, including the Security Council, to make the international system “more just, equitable, democratic, representative, effective, and efficient”. “We look forward to strengthening BRICS interaction within international parliamentary fora, including the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), to amplify the voice of the Global South,” the declaration said. Also read: A parliamentary push to the BRICS agenda On counter-terrorism, the declaration strongly condemned the April 22, 2025, terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir in which 26 people were killed and called for action against cross-border movement of terrorists, terror financing and safe havens. It urged “zero tolerance for terrorism” and called for an end to double standards in counter-terrorism efforts. The declaration also highlighted cooperation on emerging technologies including artificial intelligence and proposed a digital public infrastructure repository for BRICS countries. “We emphasise the need to strengthen the digital sovereignty of BRICS member countries by protecting data privacy and security of personal information as well as by building resilient national technological ecosystems,” it added. On climate change, member countries called for stronger mitigation and adaptation efforts. It called for stronger efforts to implement the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and its Sustainable Development Goals, while emphasising the “principle of common but differentiated responsibilities” in addressing climate change. Also read: Iran’s parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf to skip Brics forum in New Delhi Member nations also expressed concern over escalating tensions in the Middle East and West Asia, urging restraint, protection of civilians and dialogue towards lasting peace. “We reaffirm our unwavering support for the peaceful resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict based on the two-state solution, with the two States living side by side, in peace and security…” the declaration further said. Emphasising the role of legislatures, Birla said parliaments must evolve beyond law-making to become more transparent, effective and citizen-centric institutions. He also highlighted the potential of AI and digital tools to improve parliamentary research, analysis and public engagement. “Global peace truly means security, respect, justice, and the assurance of a better future for everyone—especially the younger generation,” Birla said, adding that future generations would judge current leaders by the safety and prosperity of the world they leave behind.

news.headline: 19-Month-Old Cheetah Cub Succumbs to Gunshot Wounds in Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park
news.story_lead: A 19-month-old male cheetah cub born to female cheetah Nirva died from gunshot injuries in Madhya Pradesh after being rescued from Morena district. Diagnostic scans revealed multiple firearm pellets lodged inside the cub's body, prompting the state government to form a Special Task Force to conduct a comprehensive investigation.
news.full_article_text:
### Incident Overview and Rescue Operation
A 19-month-old male cub of cheetah Nirva was rescued from the Pahargarh forest range in Morena district and brought to Kuno National Park for emergency care. Although initial reports suggested the animal had been beaten with sticks, subsequent veterinary examinations confirmed that the cheetah sustained fatal gunshot wounds.

### Medical Findings and Surgical Intervention
Diagnostic imaging performed at the Department of Veterinary Surgery and Radiology at NDVSU, Jabalpur, revealed several metallic objects within the animal's body:
- Pellets were detected near the lumbar (L1) and thoracic (T13) vertebrae, causing structural damage to the musculoskeletal and nervous systems.
- Two pellets were located in the subcutaneous tissues surrounding the left shoulder.
- One pellet was identified within the right lung parenchyma.
Veterinary surgeons extracted five firearm pellets during emergency surgery; however, the cub succumbed to its injuries on Tuesday morning.

### Circumstances Leading to the Event
According to local forest reports, the cub and another cheetah strayed into the outskirts of Bamori village in Morena, entering the courtyard of resident Somlavir Singh and killing two tethered calves. The noise alerted the family and other villagers. The injured cub was later found in the adjacent Pahargarh range. Authorities suspect the animal was shot either by a villager in retaliation or by poachers.

### Demographic Status and Institutional Response
- **Current Cheetah Population:** Following this death, India's total cheetah population stands at 58, distributed across Kuno National Park (52), Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary (4), and Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve (2).
- **Government Investigation:** The Madhya Pradesh state government established a Special Task Force (STF) combining police and forest officers.
- **Demands for Independent Probe:** Wildlife activist Ajay Dubey called for a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe, criticizing existing surveillance arrangements managed by 18 tracking teams.

hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### घटना और बचाव अभियान
मादा चीता निरवा के 19 महीने के नर शावक को मुरैना जिले की पहाड़गढ़ रेंज से बचाकर इलाज के लिए कूनो राष्ट्रीय उद्यान लाया गया था। शुरुआती रिपोर्टों में लाठियों से चोट लगने की बात कही गई थी, लेकिन पशु चिकित्सा जांच में गोली लगने से घायल होने की पुष्टि हुई।

### चिकित्सीय निष्कर्ष और सर्जरी
जबलपुर स्थित NDVSU के पशु चिकित्सा सर्जरी एवं रेडियोलॉजी विभाग में किए गए सीटी स्कैन से शावक के शरीर में कई धातु के छर्रे मिले:
- रीढ़ की हड्डी (L1 और T13 वर्टेब्रा) के पास छर्रे पाए गए, जिससे तंत्रिका और मांसपेशी प्रणाली को गंभीर नुकसान पहुंचा।
- बाएं कंधे के पास त्वचा के नीचे दो छर्रे मिले।
- दाहिने फेफड़े के पैरेन्काइमा में एक छर्रा पाया गया।
आपतकालीन सर्जरी के दौरान पशु चिकित्सकों ने शरीर से पांच छर्रे निकाले, लेकिन मंगलवार सुबह शावक ने दम तोड़ दिया।

### घटना का कारण
स्थानीय वन अधिकारियों के अनुसार, यह शावक एक अन्य चीते के साथ मुरैना के बामोरी गांव की बाहरी सीमा में घुस गया था और एक घर के आंगन में बंधे दो बछड़ों का शिकार कर लिया। शोर सुनकर ग्रामीण एकत्र हो गए। बाद में शावक जंगल में घायल पाया गया। अंदेशा है कि ग्रामीणों या शिकारियों ने उस पर गोली चलाई।

### वर्तमान चीता आबादी और जांच
- **भारत में चीतों की संख्या:** इस घटना के बाद देश में कुल चीतों की संख्या 58 रह गई है, जिसमें कूनो राष्ट्रीय उद्यान में 52, गांधी सागर वन्यजीव अभयारण्य में 4 और वीरांगना दुर्गावती टाइगर रिजर्व में 2 चीते शामिल हैं।
- **सरकारी कार्रवाई:** राज्य सरकार ने पुलिस और वन अधिकारियों को मिलाकर एक विशेष कार्य बल (STF) गठित किया है।
- **CBI जांच की मांग:** वन्यजीव कार्यकर्ता अजय दुबे ने 18 निगरानी टीमों के बावजूद सुरक्षा में हुई चूक को लेकर सीबीआई जांच की मांग की है।

hindi_translation.story_lead: भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) के डिप्टी गवर्नर के बयानों के अनुसार, भारत में 8% से अधिक की सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (जीडीपी) वृद्धि दर हासिल करने की क्षमता थी। हालांकि, अप्रत्याशित बाहरी आर्थिक झटकों के कारण अर्थव्यवस्था इस क्षमता का पूरा लाभ नहीं उठा सकी।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### आर्थिक वृद्धि की संभावना और बाहरी कारक

भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) के एक डिप्टी गवर्नर द्वारा साझा किए गए आकलन के अनुसार, भारत की घरेलू अर्थव्यवस्था में 8% से अधिक की दर से सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (जीडीपी) विस्तार हासिल करने की व्यापक क्षमता थी। यह आंतरिक गति घरेलू मांग और बुनियादी आर्थिक आधारों की मजबूती को दर्शाती है।

### बाह्य झटकों का प्रभाव

- **मुख्य बाधा:** प्रतिकूल वैश्विक आर्थिक झटकों ने अर्थव्यवस्था को 8% के स्तर तक पहुंचने से रोकने में मुख्य बाधा के रूप में कार्य किया।
- **घरेलू मजबूती बनाम बाहरी जोखिम:** जहां घरेलू आर्थिक मानदंड मजबूत बने रहे, वहीं अंतरराष्ट्रीय वित्तीय अस्थिरता और भू-राजनीतिक तनावों ने राष्ट्रीय उत्पादन वृद्धि के सामने चुनौतियां पेश कीं।
bullet_points: आरबीआई के डिप्टी गवर्नर ने कहा कि भारत की जीडीपी वृद्धि दर में 8% से अधिक होने की क्षमता थी।
प्रतिकूल बाहरी आर्थिक झटकों को इस लक्ष्य से पीछे रहने का मुख्य कारण बताया गया।
घरेलू आर्थिक बुनियादी ढांचे और मांग कारकों में पर्याप्त मजबूती बनी हुई है।
वैश्विक आर्थिक अनिश्चितताओं सहित बाहरी कारक घरेलू आर्थिक उत्पादन को प्रभावित करते रहते हैं।
